**My reasoning:**

I have been farming this land my whole life. My father farmed it before me. In Quzhou, everyone grows wheat and corn — that is what the land is for, that is what the water is for, that is what I know. I have 7 mu. At 70, my back is not what it was, so I hire a machine for planting and harvesting, but I still manage the water and fertilizer myself.

For wheat, I planted last October. I use Jimai 22 — the seed station sells it and it gives good yield. I put down compound fertilizer before tillage and topdress with urea when the wheat joints in spring. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. My neighbor tells me to use less water, but I have always done three times and my yields are steady around 450 jin per mu. I spray herbicide in winter and one more time near heading for the aphids and rust.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn straight into the stubble — no need to till. I use Zhengdan 958. My son bought it last year too, so I know where to get it. I push urea hard at the big bell stage because that is when corn needs to eat. If July is dry I run the pump once. I spray for corn borer in August.

I am not changing anything this year. Prices are uncertain, my land is familiar, and at my age, routine keeps mistakes away.
